content:
Krail stands with the unsigned order on the table between you, the pen laid neatly beside it, and waits. The silence stretches. He does not fidget; he simply watches you the way he watches a ledger line that has not yet balanced.

A knock comes at the door — two short raps. A footman leans in, soot still grey on his sleeve from the fire crews.

"Beg pardon, my lord. Master Krail — the carrier's man from the counting house is below, insisting on the quarter's shipping tallies before the wagons are released. He says he'll wait no longer than the hour."

Krail's chin lifts a fraction. For the first time this morning, something moves behind the grey eyes — a quick calculation, quickly smoothed over.

"Of course." He gathers the pen case, aligns it with his keys, and slides the unsigned order an inch toward the table's edge. "The matter will keep, my lord. The prisoners remain in your custody until the order is signed — the guards are instructed accordingly. I would note only that delay carries its own weight; the household expects discipline to be seen to be done."

He bows, precisely, the depth of it calibrated to your rank and no deeper. "I will return within the hour for your decision."

He turns to the door. As it opens, the corridor beyond shows a slice of Magerrett — she has not even pretended to be passing by; she stands close against the wall beside the door frame, arms crossed, her eyes going from Krail to you and then to Elise and Liora. Krail pauses a half-step.

"Lady Magerrett."

"Master Krail." Her voice is flat and pleasant in the way of someone who has already decided she does not like him today.

He inclines his head, steps past her, and his polished shoes recede down the passage. The footman withdraws and the door closes.

The room is different without him — smaller and quieter at once, the smell of wet ash settling back in. The ruined portrait leans against the wall where the servants set it: your mother's face still whole at the left edge, the right half gone to black char, a single painted hand surviving at the bottom of the frame.

Elise stands where the guards left her, Liora close beside her. Liora's bandaged hand is curled against her stomach; she shifts from foot to foot, and her mouth opens — then Elise's good hand settles on her shoulder, and the words stay behind her teeth. Elise smooths her apron with the motion, soot streaking the clean cloth, and lowers her head.

"Forgive her, my lord," she says quietly. "She only wants to say she's sorry. I've told her to wait till she's asked."

Isolde stands at your right shoulder, hands folded, yellow eyes moving once to the door and back to the room. Her face is its usual stillness. Nothing about her posture suggests an opinion.

The unsigned order lies at the table's edge, the approval space blank. The guards by the far wall watch you, waiting on your word for everything that happens next.
